q: Who is generally responsible for debts of a sole proprietorship?
r: The owner personally
The business and owner are legally the same.
w: Customers do not owe the business debts.
The government does not cover them.
No one, because the business is separate
A sole proprietorship has no separate liability.

q: A supplier ships goods that do not match the sample the buyer approved. What legal principle may the buyer rely on?
r: Breach of the sales agreement or warranty
The goods must conform to what was promised.

q: What is a union contract also called?
r: A collective bargaining agreement
It sets terms between workers and employer.

q: Why does a business need permits to build or remodel?
r: To ensure work meets safety and zoning rules
Permits show compliance.
w: To increase the building's value automatically

q: An employee signs a non-compete agreement that bars work in the same field anywhere for 20 years. What might a court decide?
r: The restriction may be unreasonable and unenforceable
Courts consider reasonableness.
w: It must be enforced exactly as written
It becomes void only if the employee quits
It is the same as a patent

q: Which greeting is most suitable for a formal letter to an unknown recipient?
r: Dear Hiring Manager,
It is professional and appropriate.

q: A manager gives instructions quickly, and the employee seems unsure. What should the manager do?
r: Ask the employee to restate the instructions and invite questions
Checking confirms understanding.

q: What is an effective subject line for a business email?
r: A short phrase that tells what the message is about
It helps readers prioritize.
w: A joke unrelated to the message

q: Why is it important to know your audience before presenting?
r: You can adjust content and tone to their needs
Relevance keeps attention.
w: So you can skip the introduction

q: A coworker sends a rude email. What is the best response?
r: Reply calmly and professionally or discuss in person
A calm reply prevents escalation.
w: Reply with an equally rude email
Forward it to the whole company

q: Why should employees avoid arguing with customers?
r: Arguments damage relationships and reputation
Calm service builds trust.

q: A customer repeatedly buys the same brand of coffee. What can the store do to show appreciation?
r: Offer a loyalty reward or a personal thank-you
Recognition encourages loyalty.
w: Raise the price for that customer only

q: What is the first step in handling an angry customer?
r: Listen without interrupting
Listening shows respect.

q: What do economists mean by 'demand'?
r: The quantity buyers are willing and able to buy at various prices
It reflects desire plus ability to pay.
w: The price set by the government

q: A new technology makes producing smartphones cheaper. What is the likely effect on the market?
r: Supply increases and prices tend to fall
Lower costs expand supply.

q: What is a budget deficit?
r: Government spending is greater than revenue
It must be financed by borrowing.
w: Government revenue is greater than spending

q: What is the role of the Federal Reserve?
r: Manage the money supply and interest rates
It conducts monetary policy.

q: What is it called when you put yourself in another person's position to understand them?
r: Empathy
It builds understanding.

q: A team member is frequently late with work. Which response best combines respect and accountability?
r: Discuss the issue, ask about obstacles and set clear deadlines
It solves the issue respectfully.
w: Do the work without telling anyone

q: Why is listening to different viewpoints valuable?
r: It can lead to better ideas and decisions
Diverse input improves results.
w: It wastes time in every case

q: What is an angel investor?
r: A person who provides money to a start-up in exchange for ownership
They invest early.
w: A bank that gives loans only

q: A small business owner must choose between buying a $5,000 machine or hiring a worker for $5,000 a year. What should she compare first?
r: Expected output, long-term costs and demand
Analysis guides the choice.
w: Whether competitors have the same machine only

q: What is a business incubator?
r: An organization that helps new businesses grow with space and advice
It supports start-ups.
w: A machine that warms eggs only

q: What is a check register used for?
r: Recording deposits, withdrawals and balances
It helps track an account.

q: A person has $4,000 in credit card debt at 24% APR. Which action saves the most interest?
r: Pay more than the minimum each month
Faster payoff cuts interest.

q: What is a tax deduction?
r: An amount that reduces taxable income
It lowers the tax owed.

q: What is retirement planning?
r: Saving and investing to support life after work
Early planning helps.

q: What is a probation review?
r: An early evaluation of a new employee's performance
It decides if the employee continues.
w: A review of the company's taxes

q: A company wants to improve diversity. Which action helps most?
r: Recruit from diverse communities and use fair hiring practices
Inclusive recruiting widens the pool.

q: Why do employers offer flexible schedules?
r: To attract and keep employees with different needs
Flexibility improves satisfaction.

q: A company wants to share a large file with a customer securely. Which method is best?
r: Use an encrypted file-sharing service
Encryption protects the file.
w: Post it on a public site
Leave it on a USB in a public place

q: What is the main benefit of using templates for business documents?
r: Consistency and time savings
Templates standardize format.

q: What does a marketing budget cover?
r: Money planned for advertising and promotion
It guides spending on marketing.

q: A brand sees a drop in repeat purchases after changing its packaging. What is the best next step?
r: Gather customer feedback about the change
Feedback explains behavior.

q: What is customer segmentation by geography?
r: Dividing customers by where they live
Location can shape needs.

q: What is the purpose of preventive maintenance?
r: To fix equipment problems before they cause breakdowns
It reduces downtime.
w: To replace working equipment every day
To ignore equipment until it fails

q: A manufacturer reduces batch size to avoid overstock. What is a possible downside?
r: More frequent setups and higher per-unit cost
Smaller batches can raise costs.

q: What does a safety audit do?
r: Checks that workplace safety rules are followed
It finds hazards.

q: Why is first impression important in an interview?
r: It influences how the interviewer views you
Professional appearance and manner matter.
w: It matters only after being hired

q: A coworker asks you to cover for them by lying to the manager. What should you do?
r: Decline politely and encourage honesty
Integrity matters.

q: What is outsourcing a strategic benefit of?
r: Focusing on core activities while others handle support tasks
It can improve efficiency.

q: A firm sees several competitors lower prices. Which response is most strategic?
r: Analyze costs and value, then decide whether to match, differentiate or hold
Strategy weighs options.
w: Match all price cuts without analysis
Lower quality to save cost without warning

q: What is vertical integration?
r: A company controlling several stages of its supply chain
It can reduce dependence on suppliers.

q: What is a deposition?
r: Sworn testimony taken outside the courtroom
It is used in legal cases.

q: What is insurance fraud?
r: Making false claims to get insurance money
It is illegal.

q: What is a press release?
r: An announcement sent to the media about company news
It informs the public.

q: What is the difference between fixed and variable costs?
r: Fixed costs stay the same while variable costs change with output
Rent is fixed; materials are variable.
w: Fixed costs change with output and variable costs stay the same

q: What is a mixed economy?
r: An economy with both private business and government involvement
Most modern nations are mixed.
w: An economy run only by tradition

q: What is an example of professional behavior during a disagreement?
r: Staying respectful and focusing on the issue
It keeps the conversation productive.

q: What is a franchise fee?
r: A payment to the franchisor to use its brand and system
It is often paid up front.

q: What is a credit report?
r: A record of a person's borrowing and repayment history
Lenders review it.
w: That is not a credit report.

q: What is an exit interview?
r: A conversation with an employee who is leaving
It reveals reasons and suggestions.
w: A job interview for a new hire

q: What is a software update used for?
r: Fixing issues and improving security or features
Updates keep systems safe.

q: What is an endorsement?
r: A public statement of support for a product by a person or group
Endorsers can influence buyers.

q: What is batch production?
r: Making a set number of items at one time
Batches fit certain products.
w: Making one custom item at a time
Making goods nonstop on an assembly line

q: What does it mean to demonstrate initiative?
r: Take action without waiting to be told
It shows leadership.

q: What is the purpose of a return policy?
r: To set clear rules for returns and refunds
Clear rules build trust.

q: What is purchasing power?
r: The amount of goods that money can buy
Inflation lowers it.
w: The number of stores in a country

q: What is the purpose of a business license renewal?
r: To confirm the business still meets legal requirements
Renewals keep permission current.
